Package index

Working with files downloaded from the BLS via a browser

The first way most people will pull data from the BLS will be a web form

parse_oes_download()
Read an excel spreadsheet pulled from the BLS site.

Data

Data frames included with the package because they have helpful definitions.

EDUCATIONAL_ATTAINMENT_LEVELS
Levels of educational attainment, according to the BLS
EDUCATION_ASSIGNMENTS
Education and training assignments by detailed occupation
SOC_HIERARCHY
Standard Occupational Classification

Internal

Utilities for updating package data sets or reducing repetition

Data creation

Normally, these would be in data-raw, but I don’t want to include files that are just duplicates straight from the BLS website.

parse_soc_hierarchy_file()
Read a spreadsheet of Standard Occupational Classification codes
parse_education_assignments_file()
Read a spreadsheet of S.O.C. codes and educational levels.

Utilities

Code that, while used frequently within the package, is probably not going to be relevant for end users.

dashed_soc_to_int()
Utility for converting xx-xxxx SOC codes to 6-digit integers

Glossaries

Lookup tables for understanding different abbreviations found in BLS data.

GLOSSARY_OF_AREA_TYPES
Types of geographic area
GLOSSARY_OF_AREAS
Specific geographic areas
GLOSSARY_OF_SEASONAL_ADJUSTMENTS
Types of seasonal adjustments

Survey Metadata

The BLS provides a set of tables on its public download site that explain all of the cryptic abbreviations in each survey’s data.

GLOSSARY_OF_SURVEYS
The menu of surveys at the BLS API
METADATA_FOR_LA
Lookup tables for codes used by series "LA."
METADATA_FOR_WP
Lookup tables for codes used by series "WP."
